main_text.p: des transferte, dummodò non intra octuagesimum à mari stadium : nam Carthaginem hanc delere , nobis est constitutum. Tum verò dolor ingens legatis in amentiam primùm mutatus, & voces atroces jactatæ. Mox maxstum silentium secutum , & post id lamenta, querelæ , preces, datæ fidei obtestatio, perfidiæ detestatio. Et cum proficere-tur nihil, legati in urbem reversi , expositis omnibus in furorem pene eam derunt. Sævitum verbis in primores, qui priora suaserant, & post obsides datos armis omnibus civitatem nudave-rant. Audita visaque omnia, quæ tali casui inopinato & indigno erant congrua. Rursum legati ad consules missi, ac breves inducias petitæ, per quas sup-plicatum iri Romam posset. Quod et-iam cum frustrà esset, tandem ex despe-ratione in rabiem acta civitas, iniquissi-mæ vis ac injuriæ propulsatio decreta, Asdrubal exul, qui contra patriam ex-ercitum paratum habebat, revocatus, patriæque reconciliatus. Tum hostilia utrimque accepta : in quibus apparuit, desperata pervicacia quid posset, & ro-bur Carthaginis etiam inermis quan-tum esset. Bellum enim in quartum an-num tractum, multa ab obsessis oppu-gnatisque patrata, quæ fidem pene su-perant.

page.notes: The page contains one continuous paragraph; the final word "perant." is set right-aligned at the foot of the text, so it is given as a separate closing line in the text. Long s and the ct and st ligatures are normalised to plain letters (for example "constitutum" to "constitutum", "aɛta" to "acta"). "maxstum" is printed as shown and is probably a printing error for "maximum". "octuagesimum" follows the ligature in the scan, so it is a reading, not a certain form. The strips at the right edge belong to the neighbouring page and were not transcribed.
